title: Imported chikungunya in French travelers returning from outbreak-affected regions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Outbreaks of chikungunya disease are unpredictable, typically episodic, and explosive. This study aimed to describe the rate of chikungunya in French travelers returning from La Réunion, Mayotte, Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba, all of which showed major chikungunya resurgences in 2025, and to assess the potential burden that CHIKV outbreaks—whether officially notified or not—can cause to travelers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Publicly available data from Santé Publique France were used to extract the number of chikungunya cases, and International Air Transport Association data were used for information on the number of flight tickets to estimate traveler numbers. In 2025, several such outbreaks were observed and a marked increase in imported cases of chikungunya to mainland France was reported.
analysis.methods: These data were used to derive monthly rates of imported cases of chikungunya to mainland France from January to December 2025. Methods included using publicly available data from Santé Publique France and International Air Transport Association data to estimate traveler numbers.
analysis.main_results: Trends in rates of chikungunya among travelers returning to mainland France from La Réunion and Mayotte closely mirrored the sharp and compact epidemic curves observed locally. Peak imported rates exceeded 1,800 cases/100,000 travelers (La Réunion [April]) and 400 cases/100,000 travelers (Mayotte [May]) and remained above 100 cases/100,000 travelers for March, April, May, and June (La Réunion) and April, May, and June (Mayotte). For Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba, estimated peak rates were 248, 338, 90, and 2,480 cases/100,000 travelers, respectively, although it was noted that some outbreaks were not officially notified or were reported late.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Returning travelers to mainland France from regions facing a chikungunya outbreak in 2025 showed a substantial burden of infection and gave rise to local spread of disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of robust surveillance systems and timely outbreak notification to mitigate the risk of local spread of chikungunya from returning travelers.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations in the study design or data collection methods.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the rate of chikungunya infection among French travelers returning from regions with major outbreaks in 2025, including La Réunion, Mayotte, Mauritius, Madagascar, Sri Lanka, and Cuba. The research aimed to assess the potential burden of CHIKV outbreaks on travelers, whether officially notified or not. Using data from Santé Publique France and the International Air Transport Association, the study derived monthly importation rates of chikungunya to mainland France from January to December 2025. Results showed that the trends in imported cases closely mirrored local epidemic curves, with peak rates exceeding 1,800 cases/100,000 travelers in La Réunion and 400 cases/100,000 travelers in Mayotte. For other regions, peak rates were 248, 338, 90, and 2,480 cases/100,000 travelers, respectively. The study concluded that returning travelers contributed significantly to the local spread of chikungunya, emphasizing the need for improved surveillance and outbreak notification systems. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of detailed limitations in the study design.

title: Content and Quality Analysis of Chikungunya Fever-Related Online Information on Social Media: A Cross-Sectional Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: An outbreak of chikungunya fever (CHIKF) occurred in China in 2025, and the rapid increase in new cases has drawn the attention of health authorities. The outbreak also sparked widespread discussion on social media platforms, where fear-inducing and uncertain information about CHIKF circulated rapidly online, which may complicate risk communication and outbreak management efforts.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We searched TikTok China and Bilibili using the term "chikungunya fever" and included the top 100 videos from each platform on October 9, 2025 (N = 200).
analysis.methods: Video quality was assessed using the Global Quality Scale (GQS) and the Video Information and Quality Index (VIQI); information reliability was evaluated using the modified DISCERN (mDISCERN); transparency was measured using the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark criteria; and engagement was quantified using platform-based interaction metrics.
analysis.main_results: Videos from TikTok China showed higher JAMA benchmark scores, whereas videos from Bilibili achieved comparatively higher mDISCERN scores. Subgroup analyses indicated no statistical differences in engagement metrics across uploader categories, whereas quality scores differed significantly. In addition, engagement metrics showed weak correlations with video quality or reliability.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The quality and reliability scores for CHIKF-related short videos on the two platforms were relatively low. The results support careful consideration of whether video quality and information reliability should be more explicitly incorporated into platform governance and content distribution strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for improved content governance on social media platforms to ensure accurate and reliable information about chikungunya fever is disseminated to the public.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the potential for bias in selecting top videos. The evidence is moderate as it is based on observational data and platform-based metrics.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study analyzed the content and quality of chikungunya fever-related short videos on TikTok China and Bilibili. The research aimed to assess video characteristics, reliability, transparency, and engagement. The study found that while TikTok China videos had higher JAMA benchmark scores, Bilibili videos scored higher on mDISCERN. Engagement metrics showed weak correlations with video quality or reliability. The results suggest that platform governance and content distribution strategies should incorporate video quality and reliability to improve public health communication. The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and potential selection bias, and the evidence is moderate due to reliance on observational data.

analysis.main_results: The method demonstrated the ability to rapidly recover full viral genomes from clinical and vector samples, facilitating real-time tracking of viral diversity, evolution, and spread during outbreaks.

title: Rainfall and human activities drive Aedes aegypti breeding sites infestation and larval density in urban and rural settings of Bobo-Dioulasso in western Burkina Faso

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to understand the factors driving Aedes aegypti breeding site infestation and larval density in urban and rural settings of Bobo-Dioulasso, western Burkina Faso, as these mosquitoes are the primary vector of dengue, chikungunya and Zika viruses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional survey was conducted in urban and rural sectors of Bobo-Dioulasso across dry and rainy seasons. analysis.methods: Infestation varied markedly by container type, with domestic materials, basins, and flower pots showing the highest positivity rates, whereas kettles and animal skins were rarely colonized. The study accounted for climatic variables and focused on structural characteristics of containers, exposure, and organic matter.
analysis.main_results: Domestic materials (41.9%), basins (29.4%) and flower pots (28.6%) showed the highest positivity rates, whereas kettles and animal skins were rarely colonized. Seasonality also structured larval dynamics, with more containers being positive during the dry season but mean density three-fold higher in the rainy season.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of targeting specific containers, particularly jars, barrels and tires, for interventions in areas at greatest transmission risk. Integrating rainfall-based surveillance with community-led source reduction could enhance control efforts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the confidence in the findings is moderate due to the lack of detailed statistical analyses and the potential influence of unmeasured confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the factors influencing Aedes aegypti breeding site infestation and larval density in urban and rural areas of Bobo-Dioulasso, western Burkina Faso. It also notes that seasonality affects larval dynamics, with higher densities observed during the rainy season. The findings suggest that interventions should focus on these highly productive containers, integrating rainfall-based surveillance with community-led source reduction. However, the study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the confidence in the results is moderate due to the absence of detailed statistical analyses and potential confounding factors.

title: Beyond long COVID: post-acute infection syndromes across Africa, a systematic review

analysis.research_question_and_background: Post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS) have gained global attention through Long COVID, yet many pathogens most closely linked to PAIS are endemic to Africa, where evidence remains scarce; a gap with implications for health equity and global health security.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a systematic review, searching Medline, Embase, and grey literature until 7 November 2025 for studies in Africa reporting symptoms four or more weeks after acute infection. Of 1,368 records, 65 studies were included, 42 on Ebola virus disease and 19 on chikungunya, with moderate to low risk of bias.
analysis.methods: Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data on study characteristics, symptom prevalence, clinical presentation, and associated factors.
analysis.main_results: Prevalence of PAIS ranged from 12.1% to 78.6% after chikungunya. Musculoskeletal pain, ocular complications, headache, and fatigue predominated after Ebola; arthralgia was the hallmark of post-chikungunya disease. Substantial symptom burden persisted years after acute infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The reported prevalence of persistent symptoms among survivors is high, although the absence of comparison groups in most studies complicates attribution to the infection itself.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Health systems in Africa must adapt to provide long-term survivor care, embedding follow-up into existing chronic care platforms.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: As substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies, results were summarised descriptively.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review aimed to evaluate the prevalence, clinical presentation, and associated factors of post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS) following non-COVID infections in Africa, with a focus on chikungunya virus. The study included 65 studies, 19 of which were on chikungunya, and found that PAIS prevalence ranged from 12.1% to 78.6% after chikungunya infection. Musculoskeletal pain, ocular complications, headache, and fatigue were common after Ebola, while arthralgia was the hallmark of post-chikungunya disease. Persistent symptoms were reported to persist years after acute infection, with female sex, older age, and greater acute disease severity being the most frequently associated factors. The authors highlighted the need for health systems in Africa to adapt to provide long-term survivor care, emphasizing the importance of understanding the chronic consequences of pathogens endemic to the region. However, the study's results were summarised descriptively due to substantial heterogeneity across studies, and the absence of comparison groups in most studies limits the ability to attribute symptoms solely to the infection.

title: Development of a One-Step RT-LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12b Assay for Rapid On-Site Detection of Dabie Bandavirus

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a rapid, accurate, and field-applicable diagnostic strategy for Dabie bandavirus (DBV), which causes severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) and poses a serious threat to global public health security.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study designed and optimized a one-step RT-LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12b assay for DBV detection, focusing on a conserved region of the DBV L segment, and validated it using 42 clinical specimens.
analysis.methods: LAMP primers and CRISPR sgRNA were designed based on the conserved region of the DBV L segment. The assay was optimized to operate under isothermal conditions at 60 °C, delivering results within 40 minutes. Clinical validation showed 100% sensitivity and specificity.
analysis.main_results: The assay demonstrated a limit of detection of 25.6 RNA copies per reaction and showed no cross-reactivity with other viruses.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The integrated RT-LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12b platform provides rapid and specific detection of DBV through a simplified workflow, supporting its potential application in resource-limited environments.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This assay can improve the diagnosis of SFTS, which is critical for timely treatment and control of the disease, especially in mountainous and hilly areas where people are at increased risk.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not report any design limitations or bias, and the evidence strength is high.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a rapid, accurate, and field-applicable RT-LAMP-CRISPR/Cas12b assay for Dabie bandavirus (DBV), which causes severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS). The assay demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity and can be used in resource-limited settings.
